rootCauses.title: Shadow DOM emulation exposes the composed tree through the light-DOM API: shadow content becomes host children, slotted nodes are reparented into <slot>, light-DOM comments vanish
rootCauses.area: crates/script/js/20_dom.js (shadowPrepare/shadowDistribute/lightInsert, lines 200-310, 851-898, 2637-2645), crates/script/js/30_html.js:1095-1098 (HTMLSlotElement), vendor/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:1300 (set_shadow_host) + shadow_css.rs, vendor/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:386-396 (parent_node_is_shadow_root/containing_shadow_host stubs)
rootCauses.mechanism: attachShadow / <template shadowrootmode> do not create a separate tree. shadowPrepare (20_dom.js:208) moves every light child of the host into a detached fragment (info.lightFrag); the shadow content is then inserted as the host's real children, and shadowDistribute (20_dom.js:218-244) physically appends element and text nodes from the fragment into the matching <slot> element inside that content. Comment nodes are skipped (line 234 `else if (t !== 3) continue;`) and stay in the detached fragment, so they disappear from the document. Consequences seen by page scripts: host.childNodes/children/firstChild return the shadow content (style, wrappers, slots) instead of the light children; slotted.parentNode is the <slot>, assignedSlot is null; document.querySelectorAll('slot'/'.internal') finds shadow internals from the light DOM; selectors written against the light tree (`x-card > p`) no longer match; comment anchors between light children are lost; element counts and document.styleSheets are inflated by shadow internals. Frameworks that hydrate server-rendered light DOM around web components walk firstChild/nextSibling/comment anchors (Svelte 5 `<!--[-->`, Lit SSR, React) and hit a different tree: otto.de logs two Sharko-only `https://svelte.dev/e/hydration_mismatch` and Svelte's fallback discards the SSR markup and re-renders client-side, which drops the coupon countdown text ('Gültig bis: morgen 21:59 Uhr / Zur Aktivierung', present 6x in the server HTML) and the 'Sichere dir GRATIS Versand' module. The README (crates/script/js/README.md 'Known gaps') documents the approximation; the sweep shows it is no longer benign on component-heavy sites.
evidence: repro shadow.html (declarative + imperative shadow roots): Sharko host.childNodes = '#ws style #ws div #ws', Chromium '#ws #c[ p #c] #ws'; comment anchors in host 0 vs 2; p.parentElement 'slot' vs 'x-card'; p.assignedSlot null vs slot; document.querySelectorAll('slot').length 4 vs 0; document.querySelectorAll('.wrap') 2 vs 0 (shadow internals reachable); p.matches('x-card > p') false vs true and its colour rgb(0,0,0) vs rgb(0,128,0)

otto.de live (--eval): document.querySelectorAll('slot').length 463 (Chromium 0); getElementsByTagName('*') 4720 vs 4203; console: 2x 'https://svelte.dev/e/hydration_mismatch' only in Sharko; text 'Gültig bis:' is in the server HTML (6x, inside <ft9-benefit-countdown-v1><div slot=tomorrow>) and in Chromium's DOM but no text node containing it exists in Sharko's document; 'Sichere dir GRATIS Versand' (a.to-login-link.svelte-1rf0arj inside oc-media-object-card-v1) exists only in Chromium; sweep: 18% of words missing, elements 4906 vs 3928

stern.de live: 102 <slot> elements visible from the light DOM (Chromium 0); sweep element keys 'ws-sticky-header:1/slot:1/div:1' vs Chromium 'ws-sticky-header:1/div:1' - 172 of 229 sampled Sharko elements sit under a slot segment; after stripping '/slot:n' from keys only 1 Sharko-only element remains (the other 70 Chromium-only ones are the icon issue below); elements 3889 vs 3576, document.styleSheets 62 vs 10 (shadow <style>s counted as document sheets)

code: 20_dom.js:214 moves all host children out, :241 appends slotted nodes into the slot element, :234 drops comments; ShadowRoot.innerHTML setter (20_dom.js:2637) re-parents the light fragment on every re-render; stylo.rs:390-396 report no shadow structure to Stylo, so scoping is done by rewriting selectors (shadow_css.rs) and outer page rules reach into shadow content

repro.expected:
host.childNodes lists only the light children incl. the two comment anchors; slotted

keeps the host as parentElement and has assignedSlot; no or shadow internals reachable from document.querySelectorAll; 'x-card > p' matches (green text)
repro.actual:
host.childNodes is the shadow content (style, div); comments gone;

.parentElement is the ; 4 slots and 2 '.wrap' found from the document; 'x-card > p' does not match (black text)

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high - every site built from web components with slots (design systems like otto's oc-*, stern's ws-*, Polymer/Lit sites, Shoelace, Ionic, Salesforce, YouTube) exposes a different tree to its own scripts and CSS; SSR-hydrating frameworks (Svelte 5, Lit SSR, React with declarative shadow DOM) mismatch and re-render or drop content. In the other half of the cluster handelsblatt.com (swiper-container/swiper-slide paths) and mgid.com (mgs-root) show the same slot-path signature.
rootCauses.fixSketch: Proper fix (L): real shadow trees. In blitz-dom add a shadow root node kind and `shadow_root: Option<NodeId>` on the host (NodeFlags::IS_SHADOW_HOST already exists); keep light children as the host's `children`; compute slot assignment (named/manual) into a flat-tree child list used by layout, paint, hit-testing and innerText; implement TElement::parent_node_is_shadow_root / containing_shadow_host / traversal_parent (stylo.rs:386-396) and each shadow root's stylesheet set so Stylo does native :host/::slotted scoping (drop shadow_css.rs rewriting, keep N.setShadowHost for adoptedStyleSheets). The JS layer then stops moving nodes: N.childIds/N.parent/querySelectorAll stay light-tree, HTMLSlotElement.assignedNodes reads the assignment, Element.assignedSlot works, comments survive. Interim fix (M, buys most of the DOM-API correctness): keep the composed storage but present the light tree from JS - childNodes/children/first/last/next/previous on a host skip shadow content and enumerate lightFrag+slotted nodes in source order, parentNode of a slotted node returns the host, querySelector*/getElementsBy*/TreeWalker skip shadow subtrees when rooted in the light tree, shadowDistribute also moves comment nodes (or keeps unslotted/comment nodes attached to the host in a hidden-from-layout state) so hydration anchors are preserved; selector matching across the boundary still needs the native fix.

rootCauses.title: `content: "\e902" / ""` (CSS alt text) is rejected, so icon-font ::before pseudo-elements are not generated
rootCauses.mechanism: Stylo parses the `/ <alt>` part of the content property only when the static pref `layout.css.content.alt-text.enabled` is true (counters.rs:250-255: `Token::Delim('/') if ... static_prefs::pref!("layout.css.content.alt-text.enabled")`). The pref defaults to false in stylo_static_prefs and blitz-dom's Document::new (document.rs:468-475) enables grid, columns, :has, nth-child-of and others but not this one. The whole declaration becomes invalid, `content` stays `none`, the ::before box is never created and its width/height rules do nothing. Modern icon-font CSS (IcoMoon/Fontello/Sass generators, stern.de's `[class^=icon-]:before{content:"\e9xx"/""}`) uses the alt form for accessibility, so every icon drawn this way vanishes. CSS.supports('content', '"a" / "b"') is false in Sharko.
evidence: repro content-alt.html: Sharko computed ::before content 'none' and box height 0 for .alt-empty/.alt-text/.alt-attr/.counter-alt, '"★"' with height 27 only for the plain form; Chromium '"★" / ""' etc. with height 24 for all; CSS.supports('content','"a" / "b"') false vs true

stern.de live: i.icon-search/.icon-menu/.icon-profile/.icon-caret-left have ::before content 'none', width 0, font-family stern-variable in Sharko; in Chromium content '"" / ""', font-family iconfont, display flex, 24x24/20x20 - the page's CSSOM shows the rules as `.icon-arrow-down:before{content:"\e902"/""}`; the only icon that renders in Sharko (.drawer-close-icon) has a rule without alt text

sweep stern.de: 70 Chromium-only elements after normalisation are `button/i`, `ws-link/i`, `ws-scroller/button` icons; the Sharko screenshot lacks the menu, search, profile and caret glyphs while the rest of the page matches

repro.expected: all five ::before boxes render the star (height ~24), computed content keeps the '/ alt' part
repro.actual: only .plain renders; the four declarations with '/ alt' compute to content: none and 0 height

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium-high - icon fonts generated in the last few years emit the alt form; every such site loses its icons (menus, search, close buttons), which also breaks layouts sized by them
rootCauses.fixSketch: Add `style_config::set_pref!("layout.css.content.alt-text.enabled", true)` in vendor/blitz-dom/src/document.rs next to the other prefs; check the consumer of computed `Content` in blitz (generated content for ::before/::after) renders only items before `alt_start` (Stylo's ContentItems carries alt_start; nothing after it may be laid out) and that getComputedStyle serialises `"x" / "alt"` like Chromium; add a WPT run of css/css-content/ (alt-text tests) to confirm.

rootCauses.title: @container rules never apply: container-type computes to none and query_container_size is a stub
rootCauses.area: vendor/blitz-dom/src/stylo.rs:1281-1287 (query_container_size FIXME), vendor/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:468-475 (pref layout.container-queries.enabled), style/layout re-resolution in vendor/blitz-dom + crates/engine
rootCauses.mechanism: Stylo's container-query support is behind `layout.container-queries.enabled` (false in stylo_static_prefs-0.21.0/preferences.toml:4, not set by blitz-dom), so `container-type`/`container` parse as unknown (getComputedStyle().containerType is '' and CSS.supports('container-type','inline-size') is false) and @container blocks are dropped; even with the pref, TElement::query_container_size (stylo.rs:1281) returns no size, so no condition could ever match. Sites that hide or resize component content by container width get the un-queried styles. On open.spotify.com the search field's keyboard hint is hidden by `.HYAdp74EPSxNXv5y43K2{container-type:inline-size}@container (width<360px){.rxYHNa7qp7GadJDDckeX{display:none}}` (web-player.6e84cf32.css); Sharko shows it, adding 'Ctrl Shift L' to the visible text (probe metric 'extra words'), and any component using @container for responsive layout mislays out.
evidence: repro container.html: Sharko r1 '(width < 360px)', r2 '(max-width: 360px)', r3 named container, r4 '(min-width:100px)' all unapplied (display block / black), containerType '', CSS.supports('container-type','inline-size') false; Chromium hides r1-r3, colours r4, containerType 'inline-size'

open.spotify.com live: kbd parent .rxYHNa7qp7GadJDDckeX display 'block' 132x24 in Sharko vs 'none' 0x0 in Chromium (same focus state, same hover/pointer media); the rule found in the fetched stylesheet is an @container rule on an inline-size container; no other rule mentions the class
code: stylo.rs:1285 '// FIXME: Implement container queries. For now this effectively disables them without panicking.'

repro.expected: r1, r2, r3 hidden; r4 green; n1 (no container ancestor) unchanged
repro.actual: nothing applies; container-type is not even a known property

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high on the modern web (container queries are baseline since 2023 and used by design systems and CSS frameworks); in this cluster it explains spotify's hidden-content diff; elsewhere it shows up as layout/hidden-content rather than missing text
rootCauses.fixSketch: Enable `layout.container-queries.enabled` in document.rs; implement query_container_size: return the element's last laid-out content-box size (final_layout().size minus padding/border, in Au) for the axes its container-type declares; because container-query style depends on layout, run style+layout in a loop when the stylesheet set contains @container rules (Servo/Gecko do an interleaved pass: after layout, restyle elements whose container size changed - blitz can mark descendants of resized containers with a restyle hint and re-run layout until stable, bounded to 2-3 iterations); also route `cqw/cqh/cqi/cqb` units through the same size.

rootCauses.title: Detached call of a cross-origin window's postMessage (`const i = parent.postMessage; i(msg,'*')`) throws 'Illegal constructor'
rootCauses.mechanism: A cross-origin frame's WindowProxy is emulated by a Proxy around a RemoteWindow whose methods live on RemoteWindow.prototype and recover the frame path with remoteTarget(this) (40_webapi.js:277), which throws L.illegal() when `this` is not the proxy/target. Per HTML §7.2.3.5 CrossOriginProperties, postMessage/focus/blur/close are own properties of each cross-origin Window with per-window function objects, and per WebIDL an operation of a [Global] interface called with undefined `this` uses the function's own realm global, so browsers deliver the message to that window. login.disney.com's bridge page (loaded in an iframe by nationalgeographic.com) does exactly `let i=window.parent.postMessage; i({type:"getData",value:"token"},"*"), i({type:"getData",value:"guest"},"*"), i({type:"getData",value:"bridgeParams"},"*")` and dies on the first call in Sharko, so the parent SDK never answers and the OneID flow diverges (5 Sharko-only 'Error fetching guest data: User not logged in' errors, an extra iframe).
evidence: repro pm/parent.html + pm/child.html served on two origins: Sharko results {methodCall:'ok', detached:'TypeError: Illegal constructor', detachedTop:'TypeError: Illegal constructor', wrongThis:'TypeError: Illegal constructor', ownProp:false}; Chromium {detached:'ok', detachedTop:'ok', wrongThis:'ok', ownProp:true} and both messages arrive in the parent

nationalgeographic.com sharko.log: 'Uncaught TypeError: Illegal constructor at remoteTarget (40_webapi.js:277) at postMessage (40_webapi.js:329) at A (https://login.disney.com/.../v5/bridge/web:1:3140)'; the bridge's inline script at that offset is the detached call quoted above; Chromium's console for the same page has no error
same-origin `const own = window.postMessage; own(...)` works in Sharko (the native windowPostMessage does not depend on `this`), so only the cross-origin stand-in is affected

repro.path: python3 -m http.server 8765 & python3 -m http.server 8766 in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/content-missing-b/pm, then browser http://<host-ip>:8765/parent.html --eval='JSON.stringify(window.__log)' (parent.html's iframe src points at port 8766; Chromium needs NO_PROXY=<host-ip> because Playwright routes loopback through the proxy)
repro.expected: the child's detached/top/wrong-this calls all succeed and the parent receives their messages
repro.actual: each detached call throws TypeError: Illegal constructor; only the method-call form arrives

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: medium - identity/consent/ad bridges and analytics iframes commonly alias parent.postMessage; the visible damage depends on what the parent does with the missing messages (on natgeo it is a broken login bridge, not missing page text)
rootCauses.fixSketch: In L.windowAt when a RemoteWindow is created, define own, per-window function objects on the target: `for (const m of ['postMessage','focus','blur','close']) Object.defineProperty(target, m, { value: RemoteWindow.prototype[m].bind(w), writable:false, enumerable:true, configurable:false })` (spec: these are own data properties of the cross-origin object), so identity is stable and `this` is irrelevant; keep remoteTarget for getters. Also make `has`/`ownKeys` list them and let RemoteWindow.prototype.postMessage fall back to REMOTE.get(new.target-less this) -> the bound copy handles it.

rootCauses.title: Probe artifacts: generated ids in the element key and SVG child elements make matching subtrees count as missing
rootCauses.area: tools/sitediff/probe.js (keyOf, ~line 100), tools/sitediff/run.js (error signatures, SVG filtering already added in dbf644c)
rootCauses.mechanism: keyOf uses an element's id whenever it is unique, but many ids are per-load (React useId '#FormControl--_r_1_' vs '_r_o_', react-aria '#cds-react-aria-:R…', Facebook '#mount_0_0_j6' vs '_HX', WhatsApp '#u_0_0_AT' vs '_IL', heise '#a-6491' vs '#a-1541', swiper '#swiper-wrapper-<hash>'), so the whole subtree below such an id is 'only Chromium' and 'only Sharko' at once. The sweep data was also produced with the probe version that sampled SVG children (path, g, rect), which have boxes in Chromium but not in Sharko (fixed in dbf644c after the run). Error-signature matching misses Chromium errors that lack the 'TypeError:' prefix ('Uncaught Cannot read properties of null (reading 'consent')' on heise is in both browsers but counted Sharko-only), and React #421 on coursera.org is logged by Chromium too.
evidence: re-diff of the sweep samples with SVG children removed and ids containing digits/_r_/:R normalised: facebook.com 166->0 Chromium-only elements (text 56/56 words identical), whatsapp.com 91->5 (192/192 words), github.com 8->0 (502/502 words), duolingo.com 219->0 (201/201 words), tailwindcss.com 83->1, heise.de 154->1, coursera.org 444->409 (real: layout + carousel rotation)

heise.de chromium.json errors include 'Uncaught Cannot read properties of null (reading 'consent')' (the inline kameleoon script does JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('akwaConfig-v2')).consent in both browsers); coursera.org chromium.json errors include Minified React error #421

repro.path: python re-diff in this notes file; node tools/sitediff/run.js --compare-only after the fix

rootCauses.estimatedImpact: high for the sweep's signal (5 of the 12 sites in this half have no engine-caused element difference), none for users
rootCauses.fixSketch: probe.js keyOf: treat an id as unstable when it matches /\d|_r_|:R|--[a-z0-9]{6,}/ (or when the same id differs between the two runs) and fall back to the nth-of-type path; run.js: strip a leading 'Uncaught ' / 'TypeError: ' when building error signatures; re-run Chromium references for sites whose probe was captured before dbf644c or use the compare-side SVG filter.

notes: Environment / Chromium-reference effects: nationalgeographic.com - with both browsers settled 5 s the page text matches (1606 vs 1607 words, same StackModule tree); the sweep's 'extra words' were the InlineEmail module that Chromium had not loaded yet; the Illegal-constructor bug above is real but is not what produced the diff. open.spotify.com - the sweep's Chromium run was unsettled (fonts.status 'loading', 855 elements, 0 images vs 2937 elements now); the remaining real difference is the container-query one. mydealz.de - Chromium received a different variant (React shell '#header-portal/div', skeleton placeholders, 0 ), Sharko the full server-rendered page; A/B or header-based variant, request-header agent territory. heise.de - Sharko showed the Sourcepoint consent dialog (scroll locked, scrollHeight 800) while Chromium's 24 s run showed none; content differences are news rotation (5%); minor Sharko-only difference: renders its light-DOM 'Anmelden' text (Chromium shows an icon only) - probably the custom-element/shadow issue, unverified. coursera.org - hero slide differs by rotation (Chromium got the Microsoft slide in the re-run, Sharko in the sweep); the real engine difference is the navbar flex layout (search form 1216px wide at x=16 vs 587px at x=376; div.cds-9.css-rjm5sh at x=-16 width 1280 vs x=32 width 1216; buttons overlap the hero) -> layout agent. otto.de - the 'Alle Kategorien' vs 'Inspiration' nav is an A/B experiment (class names ftnav-2029; both navs are in both HTML variants); Sharko's remaining missing product tiles ('gabor stiefelette ...') are in reco_cinema Svelte tiles - consistent with the hydration fallback but not individually verified. tailwindcss.com - document.currentScript (other agent). duolingo.com - Sharko-only error is `'showNotification' in window.ServiceWorkerRegistration.prototype` inside the site's own try/catch feature detection (ServiceWorkerRegistration undefined) - harmless, api-gaps. Timing repro (timing.html): Sharko fires no spurious resize/matchMedia change events during load and reports innerWidth 1280 from the first script; differences vs Chromium are only that IntersectionObserver callbacks, requestIdleCallback and document.fonts.ready fire before 'load' in Sharko. document.fonts is empty in Sharko on every site (FontFaceSet lists only JS-created FontFace objects, 40_webapi.js:4764) - not a content cause here but sites gating on document.fonts.check() would differ. Sharko reports inline-script error positions relative to the script element rather than the document ('https://www.heise.de/:3:8'), which slows down triage. Scratch files: probes probe-*.js, outputs out...json/.err, repros shadow.html, content-alt.html, container.html, pm/, timing.html in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sharko-browser/8d979774-b495-516b-a198-458f7b9b0b92/scratchpad/rc/content-missing-b/.
